methods.label: Intersections with parallel planes
methods.explanation: The lateral face cuts a pair of parallel planes. The lines of intersection are two corresponding edges of the top and bottom bases, and they are parallel.
methods.levelReason: Directly applies the parallel-plane intersection property from required solid geometry.

methods.label: Right angles in a lateral rectangle
methods.explanation: Each lateral face is a rectangle, so we can reason within that face. In the front face \(ABCD\), the two intersection lines are \(AB\) and \(DC\). Since \(\angle DAB=\angle ADC=90^\circ\), these same-side interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\), giving \(AB\parallel DC\). The same argument applies to every lateral face, so the answer is \(1\).
methods.levelReason: Uses only rectangle right angles and the middle-school same-side interior-angle criterion for parallel lines.
